text:
sre-bot: [INCIDENT CREATED] 2001112223 - Spike in 5xx and token queue depth on /v1/generate. Variant=halley-v2-quant. Error rate ~18% over last 5m, p95 latency 120ms -> 950ms. Region: eu-west-1. Suspect: kv-cache growth / new attention kernel.

jamie: paging @oncall — I'm taking this. anyone else seeing customer reports?

omar: lots of OOMs in gpu-agent logs referencing kv-cache growth on halley-v2-quant nodes. stack traces show repeated alloc attempts then worker restarts.

maria: support: multiple enterprise customers reporting timeouts and truncated responses. escalating to critical.

lee: can we flip traffic off halley-v2-quant and fall back to halley-v2-stable for eu-west-1? quick rollback would reduce blast radius.

jamie: agreed. mitigation plan: 1) remove halley-v2-quant from routing in eu-west-1 2) apply emergency per-key QPS caps for heavy keys 3) monitor SLOs and infra queues 4) follow up with ML infra.

jamie: executing traffic-shift to stable now:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://control.redwood.local/api/v1/routes/traffic-shift" \\n -H "Authorization: Bearer $INCIDENT_TOKEN" \\n -d '{"model":"halley","from_variant":"halley-v2-quant","to_variant":"halley-v2-stable","region":"eu-west-1","percent":100}'
```

sre-bot: deploy-bot: traffic-shift job queued id=tsj-98102

support-bot: status-page: INC-8642 created, public message queued (will be updated after mitigation).

omar: preparing emergency per-key caps for top heavy keys (list from rate_analyzer). will apply qps=1 for top offenders.

lee: I'm pushing a region-level throttle and per-key caps via console now.

jamie: marking mitigation step 1 as in-progress: disable variant + reroute. watchers: @maria @omar @lee

sre-bot: traffic-shift job tsj-98102 succeeded. halley-v2-stable now receiving 100% traffic in eu-west-1.

maria: early customer feedback: timeouts decreased, but some customers still see elevated latency on long-form responses. support is updating affected accounts.

omar: halley-v2-quant still has orphaned worker processes on 3 nodes; no traffic routed so safe to evict. scheduling cleanup.

lee: applied per-key caps for top 30 keys and a region-level rate limiter (burst=50, sustained=1000rps) for eu-west-1. should reduce queueing.

jamie: running a quick canary against halley-v2-stable (50 synthetic requests) to validate latency/quality.
```bash
for i in {1..50}; do http POST https://api.redwood-hosted/v1/generate model=halley-v2-stable prompt="canary $i"; done
```

sre-bot: canary-check: 50/50 success, p95 latency=140ms.

maria: posting customer-facing update: "We've temporarily disabled halley-v2-quant in eu-west-1 and routed traffic to halley-v2-stable. We've applied per-key caps to high-volume keys to protect the service. Engineers are investigating root cause; we'll share updates."

jamie: next actions: keep emergency throttles for 1 hour, monitor error rate and infra queue depth, omar to own root cause. handoff at +45m to @lee.

lee: I'll take the 45m handoff at 2001112503. adding context and logs to the incident doc.

omar: diving into kernel/kv-cache telemetry. initial hypothesis: new attention kernel in halley-v2-quant leaks tensor buffers under certain long-sequence patterns; will reproduce in staging and propose a hotfix. if safe, we'll reintroduce quant variant at 10% canary.

support-bot: status update: INC-8642 -> "mitigated, partial impact remains; mitigation in place" posted to status page.

jamie: any regressions observed after the routing change?

maria: no customer-facing regressions besides a minority of long requests still slower than usual. support continuing to triage those cases.

lee: leaving emergency caps in place until midnight UTC, then gradual relaxation if metrics remain stable.

jamie: assigning postmortem owners: omar (root cause & infra), maria (customer comms). please upload timelines and logs to the incident doc. closing active mitigation portion of thread; keeping incident open for follow-up.

sre-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigation): primary mitigations successful; routing reverted off halley-v2-quant and per-key caps reduced queueing. active mitigation duration ~20 minutes.

jamie: thanks everyone. documenting final notes and next steps in the incidents workspace.
